definitions: An electrochemical capacitor that has an unusually high energy density compared to common capacitors, typically 10 to 100 times greater.

A high-capacity electrochemical capacitor with capacitance values much higher than other capacitors, but with lower voltage limits, that bridges the gap between electrolytic capacitors and rechargeable batteries.
examples: The device uses a supercapacitor for quick energy bursts.
Supercapacitors are being developed for electric vehicles.
Research focuses on improving supercapacitor performance.
